Hooper & Whyld, 'The Oxford Companion to Chess' (2nd ed., OUP 1992), entry 'Albin Countergambit': "Albin Counter-gambit, 1 1 0, provocative reply to the QUEEN'S GAMBIT introduced by Cavallotti (after whom it is sometimes named) in a game against Salvioli at the Milan tournament of 1 88 1 , and reintroduced in the game Lasker-Albin, New York 1 893. Hooper & Whyld, 'The Oxford Companion to Chess' (2nd ed., OUP 1992), entry 'Nimzo-Indian Defence': "Nimzo-lndian Defence, 298. The defence was tried by ENGLISCH at Vienna 1 882, by BLACKBURN£ in 1 883 ('Not much good comes of this' he wrote), and was pioneered by NIMZOWITSCH around 1 9 1 4. Hooper & Whyld, 'The Oxford Companion to Chess' (2nd ed., OUP 1992), entry 'Dunst Opening': "Dunst Opening, 8, the HEINRICHSEN OPENING. At one time its cause was advanced by Theodore Alexander Dunst ( 1 907- 85) of New York."

Hooper & Whyld, 'The Oxford Companion to Chess' (2nd ed., OUP 1992), entry 'Nimzowitsch Defence': "Nimzowitsch Defence, 593. Known since the I 6th century, used regularly by the German player Eduard Fischer ( 1 83 1-97), this opening was reintroduced by NIMZOWITSCH. Hooper & Whyld, 'The Oxford Companion to Chess' (2nd ed., OUP 1992), entry 'McCutcheon Variation': "Mccutcheon Variation, 1 205, a line in the FRENCH DEFENCE played by John Lindsay McCutcheon ( 1 857- 1 905) of Pittsburgh against STEINITZ in a simultaneous display at New York in 1 885. After the usual continuation, 5 e5 h6 6 Bd2 Bxc3 7 bxc3 Ne4 8 Qg4, White has attacking chances on the king's-side while Black has prospects on the other side of the board. This aggressive defence, fashionable around 1 905, remains in use although less popular than the WINA WER VARIATION which has similar strategic characteristics."

Hooper & Whyld, 'The Oxford Companion to Chess' (2nd ed., OUP 1992), entry 'Urusov Gambit': "Urusov Gambit. 655, I 058, sometimes called the Keidanski-Urusov Attack, a gambit that may arise from the BISHOP'S OPENING, CENTRE GAME, PETROFF DEFENCE, or SCOTCH GAMBIT. If Black takes the pawn, 4 . . . Nxe4, White gets a compensating attack by 5 Qxd4. Although his analysis was published in Schachzeitung in 1 857, URusov had played the gambit as early as 1 853 in a game against PETROFF. Also 1 1 69, the WALKER ATTACK."

Hooper & Whyld, 'The Oxford Companion to Chess' (2nd ed., OUP 1992), entry 'Cochrane Gambit': "Cochrane Gambit, 1 068 in the PETROFF DEFENCE, originated by COCHRANE in the 1 840s. White sacrifices a knight for two pawns and a strong centre. White should not seek attack, according to STAUNTON, who played the gambit successfully, but should play a positional game advancing the PHALANX of pawns in the manner advocated by PHILIDOR. Should White establish two pawns on the fifth rank they would probably give sufficient compensation for the piece. In BRONSTEIN's opinion this gambit is worth further investigation."

Hooper & Whyld, 'The Oxford Companion to Chess' (2nd ed., OUP 1992), entry 'Petrosian Variation': "399, a line in the KING'S INOIAN DEFENCE known since the 1 920s but much used by Petrosyan in conjunction with 8 Bg5, if permitted by Black's response (sec STEIN)"

Hooper & Whyld, 'The Oxford Companion to Chess' (2nd ed., OUP 1992), entry 'Flohr–Mikenas–Carls Variation': "Flohr-Mikenas Variation, 40 (sometimes called the Carls Variation) in the ENGLISH OPENING, played in the game Flohr -Thomas, Hastings 1 93 1 -2, but known earlier (e.g. Bogoljubow-Nimzowitsch. London 1 927)."

Hooper & Whyld, 'The Oxford Companion to Chess' (2nd ed., OUP 1992), entry 'Staunton Gambit': "Staunton Gambit. 258, vigorous response to the DUTCH OEFENCE, played by STAUNTON against HORWITZ in 1 847."

Hooper & Whyld, 'The Oxford Companion to Chess' (2nd ed., OUP 1992), entry 'Philidor Variation': "Philidor Variation, 643, sometimes called the Classical Attack, in the BISHOP'S OPENING, given by Ruy LÓPEZ, and advocated by PHILIDOR as the proper way to build a PAWN CENTRE. Hooper & Whyld, 'The Oxford Companion to Chess' (2nd ed., OUP 1992), entry 'Knorre Variation': "708, a dubious line in the SPANISH OPENING played in the 1 870s by the Russian-born astronomer Victor Knorrc ( 1 840 - 1 9 1 9)"

Hooper & Whyld, 'The Oxford Companion to Chess' (2nd ed., OUP 1992), entry 'McDonnell Gambit': "McDonnell Gambit, 1 1 29 in the KING'S GAMBIT Accepted, successfully introduced by McDONNELL in the first game of his third match against HOURDONNAIS.
